method: Validates one literal name per nonblank input line, up to 200 names, 1,024 characters per line and 32,768 input characters. Full refnames require at least one slash. Both modes reject components beginning with a dot or ending with lowercase .lock, consecutive dots, ASCII controls, DEL, space, tilde, caret, colon, question mark, asterisk, open bracket, leading/trailing/repeated slashes, a trailing dot, the reflog sequence @{ and backslashes. A full refname cannot be the single @. Branch shorthand follows the additional installed-Git --branch anchors: a leading dash and exact HEAD are rejected while @ is accepted; previous-checkout syntax is never expanded. The .lock check is case-sensitive. Valid branch shorthand is also shown under refs/heads/. Results list every violated naming rule and preserve input line numbers. Repository existence, remote-host policy, refspec patterns and normalization are outside scope; nothing is stored or transmitted.

sources.title: Git documentation, git-check-ref-format naming rules and --branch behavior
